'''Eva Barbro Helen Åkesson''' (born 30 December 1961 in [[Ängelholm]]) is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] professor of [[chemical physics]] who was the [[Rector (academia)|Rector]] of [[Uppsala University]] 2012–2020. She was previously Pro-Rector of [[Lund University]].

==Career==

After taking the social sciences programme at Ängelholm Upper Secondary School, Åkesson studied chemistry at [[Umeå University]], completing her doctorate in [[physical chemistry]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Åkesson|first1=Eva|title=Isomerization dynamics in solution: a time-resolved study|date=1989|publisher=Umeå University|isbn=91-7174-420-7|url=http://libris.kb.se/bib/7615666}}</ref> She had a research position ([[postdoctoral]]) at the [[University of Minnesota]] in the US from 1989 to 1991 and was subsequently employed at Umeå University. She joined the faculty of [[Lund University]] as a researcher and teacher in 1996, later serving as director of studies in chemistry. In 2003, Rector [[Göran Bexell]] appointed her to one of the two newly established positions as Vice-Rector at Lund University, with special responsibility for undergraduate studies.

In 2008 she was invited to apply for the position of Rector, to succeed Bexell. Although [[Per Eriksson (professor)|Per Eriksson]] was appointed as Rector, the university board made it clear at an early stage that it wished to see Åkesson as Pro-Rector of the university, and she was formally appointed to this position on 15 December 2008. She was Pro-Rector 2009–2011.

In 2011 she became Professor of [[chemical physics]] at [[Lund University]].

On 11 October 2011, the University Board of Uppsala University proposed Eva Åkesson as the new Rector (formally known as ''Rectrix Magnifica'').<ref>{{cite web|title=Rekrytering av rektor och prorektor|url=http://uadm.uu.se/insidan/rektorsrekrytering|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111028025526/http://uadm.uu.se/insidan/rektorsrekrytering|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 October 2011|website=uu.se|publisher=Uppsala University|accessdate=22 February 2018}}</ref> The government decided on 24 November 2011 to appoint her Rector from 1 January 2012, succeeding Anders Hallberg. The inauguration was held on 16 December 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Waara|first1=Anneli|title=New Vice Chancellor and Deputy Vice Chancellor for Uppsala University with new year|url=http://uu.se/en/news-media/news/article/?id=1640&area=2,16&typ=artikel&lang=en|website=uu.se|publisher=Uppsala University|accessdate=22 February 2018|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726071813/http://uu.se/en/news-media/news/article/?id=1640&area=2,16&typ=artikel&lang=en|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Åkesson|first1=Eva|title=Vice-Chancellor Eva Åkesson's Programme Address at the Inauguration of the Vice-Chancellor, Grand Auditorium, Uppsala University, 16 December 2011|url=http://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:alvin:portal:record-103409|website=Alvin Portal|publisher=Uppsala University|accessdate=22 February 2018}}</ref> She was the first woman to become Rector of Uppsala University.<ref>{{cite web|title=Register of Vice-Chancellors|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/history/register-vice-chancellors/|website=uu.se|publisher=Uppsala University|accessdate=22 February 2018}}</ref>

In February 2014, eight [[Dean (education)|deans]] (faculty heads) and three vice-rectors (who head the university's Disciplinary Domains) at Uppsala university demanded that Åkesson leave her position, with allegations of a poor leadership style on her part.<ref name=unt1>{{cite news|last=Skeri |first=Niklas |url=http://www.unt.se/nyheter/uppsala/rektor-forsoker-skramma-medarbetare-2952691.aspx |title="Rektor försöker skrämma medarbetare" |date=19 February 2014 |newspaper=[[Upsala Nya Tidning]] |language=sv |accessdate=15 February 2017}}</ref> The university board (consistory) gave Åkesson their vote of confidence and she remained, while the three vice-rectors left their positions.<ref name=sr1>{{cite news|url=http://sverigesradio.se/sida/artikel.aspx?programid=114&artikel=5795766 |title=Rektor Eva Åkesson sitter kvar |last1=Nilsson |first1=Mårten |last2=Thyselius |first2=Erik |publisher=[[Sveriges Radio]] |language=sv |date=27 February 2014 |accessdate=15 February 2017}}</ref> A year later, Åkesson commented on the leadership crisis, saying that she could have prepared herself better for her position as Rector.<ref name=sr2>{{cite news|url=http://sverigesradio.se/sida/artikel.aspx?programid=114&artikel=6195146 |title=Nu talar Eva Åkesson om rektorskrisen på Uppsala universitet |last=Miller |first=Andreas |publisher=Sveriges Radio |language=sv |date=22 June 2015 |accessdate=15 February 2017}}</ref>

In 2015, Åkesson was appointed an honorary doctor at the [[University of Edinburgh]] with the motivation: 'in recognition of your outstanding contributions to Sweden's higher education and internationalization.' On October 5, 2017, the University Board (Uppsala University's board) unanimously decided to follow the recruitment group and the hearing assembly's recommendation to propose to the government to renew Åkesson's mandate as rector for another term from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2020. On January 1, 2021, she returned to her previous position at Lund University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=A Lund native in Uppsala – interview with UU's outgoing rector Eva Åkesson – Lundagard.se|url=https://www.lundagard.se/2020/12/18/en-lundensare-i-uppsala-intervju-med-uus-avgaende-rektor-eva-akesson/|work=www.lundagard.se|access-date=2021-01-14}}</ref>

=== Other Assignments ===

* Member of the Royal Scientific Society in Uppsala (KVSU) 2011
* Chair of the expert panel for the evaluation of leadership and governance at the University of Helsinki in 2008 and Aalto School of Science in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eva Åkesson - Uppsala University|url=https://katalog.uu.se/empinfo/?id=N11-2237|work=katalog.uu.se|access-date=2020-09-15|language=sv|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923073301/https://katalog.uu.se/empinfo/?id=N11-2237|archive-date=2020-09-23}}</ref>
* Member of the Swedish Institute's transparency council 2011–2019
* Inspector of Europaskolan Strängnäs 2014–
* Member of the Scientific Advisory Board, [[University of Tübingen]] 2015–
* Chair of the Matariki Network of Universities 2015–2017 (Vice Chair 2014–2015)
* Chair of Sanord 2017–2018 (Vice Chair 2014–2016)
* Member of the [[University of Tartu]] Council 2017–2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tartu Ülikooli nõukogu koosseisu kinnitamine |url=https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/321022017002 |access-date=October 11, 2025 |website=Riigi Teataja}}</ref>
* Vice Chair of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities 2017–2020
* Member of the International Advisory Board, University of Helsinki 2020–
* She has served as secretary and vice chair for the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry's (IUPAC) Committee on Chemistry Education.

=== Honors ===

* Honorary member of Uplands Nation, 2012
* Rotary Östra Uppsala, honorary member, 2014
* Lund Natural Science Student Union, honorary member, 2014
* Honorary curator, Lund nations, 2014
* Honorary doctorate from the University of Edinburgh, June 2015
* H.M. The King's Medal of the 12th size in the Order of the Seraphim for "meritorious contributions to Swedish higher education," 2018
* University of Tartu's [[Johan Skytte Medal]], 2019<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johan Skytte Medal |url=https://ut.ee/en/content/johan-skytte-medal |access-date=October 11, 2025 |website=ut.ee}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

She is the daughter of Mikko Åkesson and Barbro Lundegård and was formerly married to Henrik Hedman, an upper secondary school teacher. She lives in Uppsala.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}
